SUPPORT_HTML:
Plervo aims to make working with documents more accessible. Your support helps with development, testing, distribution and maintenance.

SECURITY_DESCRIPTION: How Plervo tests releases, distributes packages and handles security reports.
SECURITY_HTML:
Plervo Suite and Plervo PDF are experimental alpha software. Public installers support Mac with Apple Silicon and Linux x86_64.

Checks before installation

The Suite accepts packages only from the official Plervo release repository. Every PDF download is checked against its SHA-256 and release version. On Mac, the Suite also checks the bundle identifier, Maintech developer signature and Gatekeeper assessment. On Linux, it rejects archive links and unsafe paths, limits extracted size, checks the executable and installs the full payload in your user account. The previous app is preserved until its replacement is ready. Downgrades are refused. On Mac, uninstall moves only the app to Trash; if that fails, it stays installed. On Linux, uninstall removes only the managed PDF payload and refuses while PDF is running. Documents and preferences are kept.

What we test

Automated checks cover the release catalogue, downloads, interrupted transfers, cancellation, rollback, signatures, versions and language selection. The Mac installer also goes through Apple notarization and malware scanning. PDF editing, save/reopen, forms, encryption and redaction are tested with synthetic documents. The previous PDF baseline completed 188,495 fuzz runs in 15 minutes with no observed crash or hang; that is a test result, not a security guarantee.

Official packages

The Mac publisher is Maintech Solutions LLC. Get installers and SHA-256 checksums from the official alpha release. The Suite manages PDF updates; updates to the Suite itself come from this website.

Known limits

Use copies of important documents. Clean-machine Mac installation and wider device coverage still need testing. Windows still requires confirmed SignPath approval and native Suite acceptance. Linux package installation, Suite/PDF rendering, update and removal were tested in isolated Ubuntu 24.04/26.04, Debian 13 and Fedora 44 containers with an X11 virtual display. Native Wayland sessions, other distributions and Linux ARM64 remain untested. PDF OCR currently targets English. Some Chinese and Telugu PDF interface characters may need system font fallback. The Suite interface supports English, Portuguese and Spanish, selected from the operating system by default.

No audit or malware scan guarantees the absence of vulnerabilities. Read the release notes for the exact tested scope.

Report a vulnerability

Use the private security channel on GitHub and choose “Report a vulnerability”. Include the version, operating system and steps using a test document. Never post passwords or personal documents in public issues.
PRIVACY_DESCRIPTION: Privacy on the Plervo website and in the PDF alpha.
PRIVACY_HTML:
This website

This site has no advertising cookies, analytics, forms or PDF uploads. Cloudflare, our hosting provider, may process technical connection details such as IP addresses to deliver and protect the pages.

Language and download suggestions

English is the default. Language links open the equivalent page in Portuguese or Spanish; your choice stays in the URL as you browse. We do not store it in cookies or local storage.

Operating-system suggestions use information already exposed by your browser, on your device. This information is not stored or transmitted. The suggestion does not identify your processor; check compatibility before downloading.

The app

PDF editing and bundled OCR run on your computer. Choosing “Check for updates” contacts GitHub for release information; it does not upload your PDF. Opening external document links or the support page uses your browser and the destination service. Local automation is disabled by default: the UI control channel must be explicitly enabled, is restricted to loopback and requires a session token. The separate command-line MCP interface also requires an explicit launch.

External services

Downloads are hosted on GitHub. The voluntary support link opens Ricardo Bonetti’s page, the creator of Plervo, on Buy Me a Coffee. Their privacy policies apply when you visit them.

Updated on October 15, 2026.

Plervo Suite

The Suite contacts GitHub at startup and when you check for updates to read public release information. Installing an app downloads its package from the official Plervo repository. It does not upload your documents, require a GitHub account or install a background service. Donation links open only when you choose them.
ABOUT_TITLE: Our own identity. An open foundation.
ABOUT_DESCRIPTION: The Plervo Suite, its open-source foundations and credits.
ABOUT_HTML:
Plervo is an independent project by Ricardo Bonetti. Plervo Suite is the starting point: install it, then choose Plervo PDF from its catalogue.

The Suite combines an original Plervo interface with installation components adapted from ArtCraft Launcher 0.4.1. Plervo PDF is based on PdfCraft 0.8.0. We preserve the authors’ credits and MIT/Apache-2.0 licences. Third-party fonts, icons and libraries retain their own licences.

A small, honest start

The first Suite catalogue contains Plervo PDF. Other apps will appear only when they are ready. Public downloads cover macOS Apple Silicon and Linux x86_64. Windows remains in preparation. The Suite manages PDF updates; updates to the Suite itself are downloaded from this website.

Both apps are experimental alpha releases. See release notes and limitations and the source code.

Plervo is not affiliated with Adobe or the ArtCraft team. Adobe and Acrobat are trademarks of their respective owners.
